prompt: Write a ~300-word piece of literary short fiction about: a bell that rings a day early. Prose only, no headings.
text:
The iron bell hung heavy against the slate gray sky of St. Jude's tower, its bronze surface etched with centuries of soot and rain. It had been silent for six hours past midnight when it suddenly shuddered in its frame. The metal groaned, a deep, tectonic sound that vibrated through the floorboards below before erupting into a clear, resonant toll. One hour earlier than scheduled, one full rotation of the earth less complete, yet there stood no clock tower to mark such precise deviation.

Below, in the narrow alleyway where Mrs. Gable slept with her ear pressed against the timber wall, eyes snapped open at the jolt. She did not rise immediately; instead, she lay frozen, listening as the single note decayed into a long, hollow hum that seemed to stretch time itself thin. Outside, the world remained in its nocturnal slumber. The streetlamps flickered weakly against the encroaching dawn, casting long shadows of sleeping cats and empty cart wheels onto the wet cobblestones. But inside the tower, the mechanism had spoken a truth too early for humanity to digest.

A baker named Thomas woke from his heavy cot halfway up the stairs leading out of the cellar, clutching a half-formed loaf of sourdough. He stared at the rising sun that now breached the eastern edge of the sky, painting the dust motes in hues of violent orange and bruised purple. "The day," he whispered to himself, feeling absurdly late for his morning routine despite having missed hours of sleep. The rhythm of life had been violently reset by a piece of cast iron swinging from above. Birds stopped their soft chirping mid-song as if startled by an invisible command; they huddled in the gutters until the second stroke confirmed that noon was approaching with frightening speed.

In this liminal space between yesterday and today, where physics seemed to bow before superstition, Mrs. Gable sat up and rubbed her temples. The world felt unmoored, as if gravity had taken a holiday while the sun advanced its own schedule without consultation. They were all waiting for something that would never arrive on time, trapped in a paradoxical moment of eternal anticipation. Yet, with each passing minute, the sky deepened into noon's harsh clarity, and eventually, they simply stood up again. The bell had rung early, but life continued anyway, adjusting its gait to meet the light it could no longer delay.
topic: a bell that rings a day early
